extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent agents and examiners in India
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines covering what is and is not patentable under Indian law, and the procedural/documentary requirements and precautions for filing patent applications in India (including provisional, complete, convention, PCT and divisional applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance obtained by mere admixture (3(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: mixture of sugar and colorants (soft drink) and simple mixtures of different medicines are mere admixtures and not patentable. Exception: an admixture resulting in synergistic properties (e.g., soap, detergent, lubricants, polymer compositions) is not considered a mere admixture and may be patentable. A process producing a substance that only aggregates component properties is also not patentable. In general, substances produced by mere admixing (or processes producing them) must show a synergistic effect to be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere arrangement, re-arrangement or duplication of known devices (3(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere arrangement or re-arrangement or duplication of known devices each functioning independently of one another in a known way is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere juxtaposition of known integers performing their own functions independently (e.g., floor mill with sieving means, umbrella with fan, bucket with torch, clock and transistor in one cabinet) is not patentable. If the collocation produces a working interrelation yielding a new or improved result, that interrelation may constitute patentable subject-matter. Arbitrary selection/juxtaposition of known features from many combinations is not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of agriculture or horticulture (3(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A method of agriculture or horticulture is excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-patentable methods: producing a new form of a known plant via modification of natural conditions, treating soil to improve it (e.g., treating soil with specified phosphorothioates to improve soil with nematodes), methods for producing mushrooms or cultivating algae. (Cited cases show such methods held not patentable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of treatment of humans or animals (3(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any process for the medicinal, surgical, curative, prophylactic, diagnostic, therapeutic or other treatment of human beings or of animals is excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: methods for treating malignant tumor cells, removal of dental plaque, prophylactic treatments like vaccination are considered therapy and excluded. Cosmetic applications are not treatment unless they arrest/cure disease or correct malfunction (case-by-case). Instruments/apparatus for surgical/therapeutic/diagnostic use may be patentable. For diagnosis, ask: (a) does the method unaided indicate whether a person/animal is suffering from a disorder? and (b) does it identify the disorder? If both yes, method is diagnosis and not patentable. Surgery defined broadly (includes manipulation). Methods of diagnosis performed on removed tissues/fluids are not excluded; methods carried out while material remains in living communication with the body are excluded. Case law examples and nuance provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plants and animals and essentially biological processes (3(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants and animals, in whole or any part thereof other than microorganisms (including seeds, varieties and species) and essentially biological processes for production or propagation of plants and animals are not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clones and new varieties of plants are not patentable. However, processes/methods of preparing genetically modified organisms (GMOs) can be patentable subject-matter. Guidelines for biotechnological inventions are provided in Annexure 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical or business methods and computer programs per se (3(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: A mathematical or business method or a computer program per se or algorithms are excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims framed as a 'computer program product', 'computer-readable medium having a program recorded thereon', etc., are treated as software per se and not patentable. Examples of excluded subject-matter: schemes or methods of bookkeeping, business methods (accounting, tax collection), contents display methods, certain methods for controlling/communicating via Internet, etc., when they are essentially computer programs. Conversely, methods that use computer programs as part of an allowable technical implementation (i.e., not 'programs as such') may be allowable. Examples of non-allowable 'programs solely intellectual in its context' include methods of executing a program that detect changes and retrieve replacements, or tools for generating new programs. Annexure 2 gives guidelines for computer-related inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works (3(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works or any other aesthetic creation whatsoever (including cinematographic works and television productions) are excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: writings, music, paintings, sculptures, computer programs (as literary works), electronic databases, books, lectures, choreographic works, cinematographic works, architecture, translations, adaptations, multimedia productions, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere scheme, rule, mental act or method of playing a game (3(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere scheme or rule or method of performing a mental act or method of playing a game is excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: method of learning a language, method of playing chess, methods of teaching, methods of learning, and broadly methods that are outcomes of mental processes. (Document also lists 'method of operating a machine or equipment' as example contextually; examine case law for boundary.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of information (3(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: A presentation of information is excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers any manner, means or method of expressing information visually, audibly or tangibly by words, codes, signals, symbols, diagrams or other modes of representation. Example: a speech-instruction means in printed text where formatting indicates stress or rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topography of integrated circuits (3(o))
rubrics_metrics.description: Topography (three-dimensional configuration) of integrated circuits is excluded from patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: three-dimensional configuration of electronic circuits used in microchips and semiconductor chips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional knowledge and mere aggregation/duplication of known properties (3(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known components is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed invention is essentially known traditional knowledge, or merely aggregates known properties of traditional components without inventive contribution, it falls outside patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions relating to atomic energy (S.4 / Atomic Energy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent shall be granted for an invention relating to atomic energy falling within subsection (1) of section 20 of the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 20(1) gives Central Government power to exclude inventions useful for or related to production, control, use or disposal of atomic energy or prescribed substances. 'Atomic energy' defined as energy from atomic nuclei (fission/fusion). 'Prescribed substances' (e.g., uranium, plutonium, thorium, beryllium, deuterium and derivatives) are listed in schedules and may be amended by central government notification. Guidance includes official letters and schedule of substances historically declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to apply (S.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent may be made by: (a) the true and first inventor, (b) his/her assignee, or (c) legal representative of deceased inventor or assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations: 'true and first inventor' excludes first importer or a person to whom invention was first communicated from outside India; applicant should disclose name, address, nationality of true and first inventor. Assignee may be natural or non-natural person (company, research org, institute, government); proof of right (assignment deed) should be submitted. Legal representative must file death certificate as proof. Applicant must be national of India or a convention country; prescribed fees differ for natural persons vs others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to apply — jurisdiction (Rule 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application must be filed in the patent office having territorial jurisdiction determined by: (a) place of residence, domicile or business of the applicant (first mentioned in joint applications), (b) place from where the invention actually originated, or (c) address for service in India given by applicant when no place of business or domicile in India (Rule 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign applicant must provide an address for service in India; an applicant may give the Patent Agent’s address as address for service.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apply — required documents and forms (Rules 6–9, 13, 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application (Form 1) in duplicate must be accompanied by specified documents: provisional or complete specification and drawings (Form 2), statement and undertaking regarding foreign filings (Form 3), declaration as to inventorship (Form 5) where applicable, priority document (if convention), power of attorney (Form 26) if filed via patent agent, proof of right if application by assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees differ (example: Rs.1000 for natural person, Rs.4000 for others) and can be paid within one month (Rule 7(2)(c)). Proof of right may be produced in the body of the application (endorsement in Form 1) or by separate assignment deed; if application by legal representative, death certificate required. Proof of right may be submitted within three months of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional specification — nature, content and timeline (4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional specification is a disclosure describing the nature of the invention; it must contain title and description, start with preamble 'The following specification describes the nature of the invention.' Claims need not be included. It is not a mere rough draft; provisional and complete specifications are permanent and independent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional spec should set forth object of invention, statement of principle/discovery and general statement of actual invention; include as much information as the applicant has. Filing a provisional gives a filing date and up to twelve months to file complete specification (though complete spec can be filed earlier). Provisional specification cannot be used for divisional, convention or PCT-designating-India applications (these must be accompanied by complete specification). Failure to file complete specification within time leads to abandonment unless request for postdating is filed on or before expiry of 12 months. Where multiple cognate provisional specs exist, applicant may request to file a single complete specification if they constitute a single invention; complete spec timing is computed from earliest filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and undertaking regarding foreign applications (S.8 / Form 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant is prosecuting an application outside India for the same or substantially the same invention, he must file a statement and undertaking (Form 3) along with his Indian application or within three months (U/S 8(1), U/R 12(1A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 3 must state detailed particulars of foreign applications (country, application number, status) and an undertaking to keep the Controller informed in writing, up to grant of the Indian complete specification, of such particulars of any subsequent foreign applications within three months of filing. Controller may require further details during pendency; applicant must furnish info within three months of request. Delay can be rectified by seeking extension via petition under Rule 138.

rubrics_metrics.name: General precautions for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should avoid actions that jeopardize patentability, such as publication or public/commercial use of the invention before applying, and should clarify rights vis-à-vis employers/co-workers/contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication (even by inventor) normally bars subsequent patenting except in rare circumstances. Public use or commercial public use prior to filing can be fatal. Secret working by reasonable trial/experiment or confidential disclosure may not destroy novelty. Delay in filing risks others filing first or independent publications; advisable to file as soon as invention has definite shape (provisional specification permitted). Clarify ownership/rights to avoid litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications (ordinary, convention, PCT, national phase, patent of addition, divisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different application types have specific definitions, requirements and effects: ordinary application, convention application (priority within 12 months), PCT international application, PCT national phase entry (within 31 months), application for patent of addition, and divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convention application must be filed in India within 12 months of first filing in convention country and be accompanied by a complete specification and priority documents (with translation if necessary); multiple priorities require multiple fees. PCT international application gives international filing date and late national entry rights; Indian Patent Office is receiving office for nationals/residents. PCT national phase: can enter within 31 months; Form 1A preferred; documents filed with application treated as complete specification. Patent of addition: for slight modifications to an existing invention; no separate renewal fee during main patent term; expires with main patent unless made independent per S.54; must reference main patent/application number and state it is an improvement/modification. Divisional application: when parent claims more than one invention, applicant may divide; priority date same as parent; complete specification of divisional must not add matter beyond parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and drawings requirements (Form 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisional/complete specification is submitted in Form 2; first page should contain the title of the invention, name/address/nationality of applicants, and a preamble to the description. Complete description should start from second page and include claims; abstract should follow signature; drawings (if any) may be attached thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and provisional specifications are distinct documents; the complete specification must include claims for which protection is required and an abstract. The provisional specification has more limited content (see provisional spec rubric).
